Ok, rant is over so I try to give you my objective indicators for bad (or a total lack of any) programming style.

  1. Biggest flaw: If you put your graphic settings to highest so your pc is dying you recognize the mouse lags behind. This indicates that the UserInterface(UI) is not separated from the engine. This causes a shitload of problems and should NEVER be done. But if you don't be strict following some sort of Model View Controller(MVC) pattern you end up like this. The MVC pattern says that you should separate the UI(Design, Icons, ...) from the Model(Data like money of player xy, research progress of tank xy) and the controller(Does the actions like Player XY pushed button(View) xy so add 22 rockets(Model) to his plane).
  2. You might recognize that you can't join a squad if your not connected to the chat. So the chat get's abused by the squad system. This is also really really really bad coding. This functionality has to be in the network code and not in the chat.
  3. If you switch research goals before you played one match the experience doesn't work and you get no experience at all. Also if you finished researching a new vehicle and has to choose the next one it often happens that you are click on the other vehicle to be researched but some other vehicle get the research progress. This is because there is no well thought-out way how to handle things. I bet there are just a bunch of functions which gets called trying to achieve the desired effect which in most cases work but not on occasions like new bought/researched vehicles. In good code you just have to call the method which does this functionality and that's it.
  4. You have to restart the game to change graphic settings. This is ok for a little indie game but not for a high budget title. It's an indicator that the game is programmed very strict and static. This has the advantage that even inexperienced programmers can write code without having to know the whole software concepts and patterns which are used, BUT it restricts the flexibility to change or replace parts. Also the mix of ingame settings and launcher settings is just terrible.
  5. If you ever had a look at the patchlog you might recognize that it most of the time: "Changed something here, something there, maybe this is now fixed ..." This indicates that there is a lack of organization. Normally you have a ticket system where every problem gets a ticket with a priority and a status(open, working on, closed, ...) So if you want to make a patchlog you just copy every ticket since the last patch which is closed now and that's it. A lot of high quality games do this automatically, you recognize this by the clearly computer generated style. ... but on this point I'm not 100% sure, because I can't really imagine that they don't use a any work distribution system. They probably are just not using it diligent.

The main point is still the lack of quality, bad coding or UI are just the side effects.

So that are just the really obvious things, if you have questions feel free to ask :)
